description: A sequencer of twenty stored voltages, ten in section A and ten in section B, each typed in on its own row. A scene manager stores whole sets of the twenty and steps between them

params.text: Goes back to the first scene
Switches the row inputs on, so they are taken instead of the stored voltages
Stores the voltages now on the panel as a new scene at the end
Writes the voltages now on the panel over the current scene
Puts the current scene's voltages onto the panel
Goes to the scene after the current one
Goes to the scene before the current one
Goes to a scene by number
Sets every stored voltage to a random value
Stores the voltages now on the panel as a new scene before the current one

inputs.text: A voltage for that row, taken instead of the stored one while ENABLE IN is switched on
A pulse stores the voltages now on the panel as a new scene at the end
A pulse writes the voltages now on the panel over the current scene
A pulse goes back to the first scene
A voltage switches the row inputs on and off
A voltage chooses which scene is the current one
A pulse goes to the scene after the current one
A pulse goes to the scene before the current one
A pulse goes to a scene by number
A CV changing the glide time applied to every row of section B
A pulse sets every stored voltage to a random value
A pulse stores the voltages now on the panel as a new scene before the current one

outputs.text: The voltage stored for that row

notes: dragging a value display with the command or windows key held sets every display of that kind at once, so all ten portamento times take the value being dragged to
menu: Use Old Portamento Scaling — reads the portamento displays on the older scale; the scale used by default spreads more time across the settings from 0.00 to 0.30
